name: Phyllis Schlafly
role: American conservative activist, founder of Eagle Forum and leader of the campaign against the Equal Rights Amendment (1924–2016)
summary: Schlafly was a conservative Republican activist who led the campaign that stopped ratification of the Equal Rights Amendment, arguing that it would remove husbands’ financial obligation to support their families and expose women to combat and the draft. Local texts record only a few of her words, so most positions are left open for the web phase.

abortion-legal.rationale: Called Roe v. Wade an illegitimate decision with no basis in the Constitution and the Casey defense of it "macabre".

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Wrote "We want immigrants to come to America and become Americans; we want patriotic assimilation."

assisted-dying.rationale: Condemned federal appeals courts for inventing a right to assisted suicide.

decide-locally.rationale: Wrote that driver's licenses are in the exclusive jurisdiction of the states and "the diversity of federalism is part of what we call freedom."

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Attacked the ruling admitting women to the all-male Virginia Military Institute and the Court's denial of inherent differences between men and women.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Opposed ceding sovereignty to global governance and urged rejecting UN treaties.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Defended Proposition 209, ending affirmative action, and attacked the judge who overturned it.

equal-conscription.rationale: On CNN in 2008 she said women do not want to be treated the same as men in the military and in combat, which rejects equal draft obligations.

equal-parenting.rationale: Supported a presumption of shared parenting in which divorced parents divide time and authority equally.

free-trade.rationale: Argued that U.S. trade agreements bring offshoring and de facto foreign trade barriers.

limit-guns.rationale: Attacked a UN plan for a global gun registry as aimed at confiscating private guns and defended the Second Amendment.

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: Called "humanitarianism" an excuse for interventionist escapades rather than U.S. strategic interests.

more-religion-public.rationale: Asked candidates to withdraw federal court jurisdiction over acknowledgment of God in public places, including the Pledge and Ten Commandments.

nation-first.rationale: Criticized "internationalism" in place of policies based on what is good for America.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Objected to deferring to international "obligations" even where they conflict with the Constitution or lack Senate ratification.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Called for deporting some ten million illegal aliens and ending birthright citizenship for their children.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Said judges had no authority to change the definition of marriage and urged the people to defy a court ruling legalizing same-sex marriage.

separate-church-state.rationale: Pressed candidates to bar court challenges to the Pledge, Ten Commandments displays and crosses in public places.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Denounced the death tax as confiscation and urged raising its exemption to $10 million.

traditional-family.rationale: Backed a federal marriage amendment and defended traditional marriage of husband and wife.

notes: Local phase: MediaSum (NPR, CNN) and the reference library searched; she never sat in Congress, so no Voteview record. Only one statement is settled by her own local words; the web phase searches the rest (family, abortion, marriage, immigration, ERA, judiciary, foreign policy).
